rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier discussions fail when they confuse real, ontological relations with conventional relations and apply legislative or social principles to creation.
rows.anchor: لم يفرقوا في هذه المباحث جهاتها الحقيقية من جهاتها الاعتبارية، ولم يفصلوا التكوين عن التشريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A created thing is good in itself; harm and ugliness arise only through its relation to other beings, when it disrupts order or deprives them of good.
rows.anchor: وجوده النفسي من غير إضافة - لا يكون إلا خيرا ولا يقع إلا حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine wisdom ensures that harmful beings yield benefits exceeding their harm, as these cited verses affirm creation’s goodness and praise.
rows.anchor: أن ينتفع من هذه الموجودات المضرة الوجود بما يربو على مضرتها وذلك قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation forms an interconnected whole: making or repairing a part entails the whole, while differences and relations among parts sustain the world’s existence.
rows.anchor: عالم الصنع والإيجاد على كثرة أجزائه وسعة عرضه مرتبط بعضه ببعض معطوف آخره إلى أوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opposites make their counterparts intelligible: without evil, loss, weakness, and hardship, good, health, possession, strength, and perfection would have no concrete instances or meaning.
rows.anchor: ولولا الشقاء لم تكن سعادة، ولولا المعصية لم تتحقق طاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience requires the possibility of disobedience; otherwise action would be necessary, eliminating the command and then obedience, praise and blame, reward and punishment, religion, and human society.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يمكن عدم الامتثال الذي هو المعصية لكان الفعل ضروريا لازما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s call to evil is a pillar of the human order of free choice and an edge that makes the straight path a path, since a boundary distinguishes its middle.
rows.anchor: وهو كالحاشية المكتنفة بالصراط المستقيم الذي في طبع هذا النوع أن يسلكه كادحا إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration story depicts real relations among humanity, angels, and Iblis through the narrative of command, obedience, pride, expulsion, and dialogue; objections arise from neglecting its meaning.
rows.anchor: وجدتها صورة منبئة عن الروابط الواقعية التي بين النوع الإنساني والملائكة وإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters call the prostration command and tree prohibition ontological, but Tabataba’i rejects this: such commands cannot be disobeyed, while both Iblis and Adam disobeyed.
rows.anchor: الأمر والنهي التكوينيين لا يقبلان التخلف والمخالفة، وقد خالف إبليس الأمر وخالف آدم النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As explained earlier in the discussion of al-Baqara, God placed Adam in a heavenly intermediate garden before earthly life and legal responsibility to test human nature.
rows.anchor: خلق جنة برزخية سماوية، وأدخل آدم فيها قبل أن يستقر عليه الحياة الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden was neither the eternal paradise from which no one exits nor an ordinary worldly home governed by legislative commands.
rows.anchor: ولا الدار كانت دارا دنيوية يعاش فيها عيشة دنيوية يديرها التشريع ويحكم فيها الأمر والنهي المولويان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden manifests human disposition generally, not Adam’s disposition as an individual; humanity must mature on earth under commands and prohibitions and attain happiness through obedience.
rows.anchor: بل كانت دارا يظهر فيها حكم السجية الإنسانية لا سجية آدم عليه السلام بما هو شخص آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an gives little detail about Iblis, identifying him as a jinn and reporting his origin in fire, without explaining his later state or the details of his creation.
rows.anchor: كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis works through human emotional drives, including fear, hope, expectation, desire, and anger, and then through the thoughts and intentions that arise from them.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أنه يتصرف فيهم من جهة العواطف النفسانية من خوف ورجاء وأمنية وأمل وشهوة وغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He decorates false and ugly things with attractive embellishments; for example, desire makes adultery seem appealing and weakens awareness of its danger until the person commits it.
rows.anchor: كالزنا مثلا يتصوره الإنسان وتزينه في نظره الشهوة ويضعف بقوتها ما يخطر بباله من المحذور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person experiences satanic suggestions as thoughts of their own and produces them in their own mind, while Satan also casts them there; ordinary external prompting would instead undermine independent thought and responsibility.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان هو الذي يوجد هذه الافكار والاوهام في نفسه كما أن الشيطان هو الذي يلقيها إليه

rows.speaker: الشيطان
rows.claim: At Judgment, Satan says God’s promise was true but his own promise false, and that he only called people, who answered him; they must blame themselves, not him.
rows.anchor: فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God denies Satan any authority except over those who follow him, matching Satan’s admission that he could only invite people.
rows.anchor: فنفى سبحانه سلطانه إلا في ظرف الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s influence on human perception is longitudinal: it works through the person and remains attributable to that person, unlike an external influence that would displace human agency.
rows.anchor: فإن تصرفه في إدراك الإنسان تصرف طولي لا ينافي قيامه بالإنسان وانتسابه إليه انتساب الفعل إلى فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan can shape every worldly attachment by disguising falsehood as truth and diverting people from the real life, through deception and embellishment.
rows.anchor: فيضع الباطل مكان الحق ويظهره في صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness of God’s true station is the source to which every sin resolves, and the heedless are described as worse than cattle.
rows.anchor: ويؤدي ذلك إلى الغفلة عن مقام الحق وهو الأصل الذي ينتهي ويحلل إليه كل ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s governance makes people’s own independence, false beliefs, and corrupt ideas seem self-generated, so they enter his authority without realizing it.
rows.anchor: فاستقلال الإنسان بنفسه وغفلته عن ربه وجميع ما يتفرع عليه من سيئ الاعتقاد ورديء الأوهام والأفكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan and his company are unseen by humans, and God has made them patrons of those who do not believe.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s guardianship over sinners and wrongdoers parallels the angels’ guardianship over those who obey and draw near to God.
rows.anchor: وولاية الشيطان على الإنسان في المعاصي والمظالم على هذا النمط نظير ولاية الملائكة عليه في الطاعات والقربات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses all and is the true guardian; no one else is a guardian or intercessor apart from Him.
rows.anchor: والله من ورائهم محيط وهو الولي لا ولي سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term احتناك means to bridle and control Satan’s followers as a rider controls a bridled mount, directing them to obey without resistance.
rows.anchor: أي لألجمنهم فأتسلط عليهم تسلط راكب الدابة الملجم لها عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan has troops who assist his work; their whispering is counted as his own work, just as the appointed messengers’ work of taking souls is attributed to their chief.
rows.anchor: إنما صنعهم صنع نفس إبليس ووسوستهم نفس وسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s references to the Angel of Death and then to God’s messengers taking souls illustrate how the acts of agents can be attributed to their appointed leader.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s host includes both jinn and humans, as the summary says his helpers include jinn, humans, and offspring of different kinds.
rows.anchor: لإبليس أعوانا من الجن والإنس وذرية مختلفي الأنواع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis has offspring who serve as his helpers and soldiers, though the Qur’an does not explain how they descend from him.
rows.anchor: أن له ذريه هم من أعوانه وجنوده لكن لم يفصل كيفية انتشاء ذريته منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between Satan’s ‘horse’ and ‘foot’ indicates variation in strength and weakness, and especially in speed of action.
rows.anchor: وهو الاختلاف من جهة الشدة والضعف وسرعة العمل وبطؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s agents also differ in whether they act collectively or individually.
rows.anchor: في العمل، وهو الاجتماع عليه والإنفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is a created, conscious, willing being who calls people to evil and pushes them toward disobedience.
rows.anchor: أن إبليس لعنه الله موجود مخلوق ذو شعور وإرادة يدعو إلى الشر ويسوق إلى المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He shared a rank with the angels and was not distinguished from them until after humanity was created, when he took the side of evil and corruption.
rows.anchor: كان في مرتبة مشتركة مع الملائكة غير متميز منهم إلا بعد خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is one cause of human deviation toward misery, error, sin, and falsehood; angels are correspondingly a cause of guidance toward happiness, perfection, and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: انحراف الإنسان عن الصراط المستقيم وميله إلى جانب الشقاء والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His varied helpers work across human worldly affairs by making falsehood look true and ugly deeds appear beautiful.
rows.anchor: بإظهار الباطل في صورة الحق، وتزيين القبيح في صورة الحسن الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s helpers act on the human heart, body, and worldly affairs such as wealth and children, jointly or separately, quickly or slowly, directly or through intermediaries.
rows.anchor: وهم يتصرفون في قلب الإنسان وفي بدنه وفي سائر شؤون الحياة الدنيا من أموال وبنين وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not perceive Satan’s agents or their acts, only themselves and their own deeds; those agents therefore do not compete with human action or exist alongside humans on the same causal plane.
rows.anchor: ولا يشعر الإنسان في شيء من ذلك بهم ولا أعمالهم بل لا يشعر إلا بنفسه ولا يقع بصره إلا بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After restating that Iblis is a jinn created from fire, Tabataba’i suggests that his first and last existence may differ.
rows.anchor: وكأن أول وجوده وآخره مختلفان

rows.speaker: اللعين
rows.claim: A debate reportedly preserved in the Torah, relayed through al-Shahrastani from a commentator on the Four Gospels, has Iblis ask why God created beings knowing some would enter Hell, imposed needless duties, ordered prostration to Adam, punished refusal, empowered him to mislead humanity, and granted him a long reprieve despite evil.
rows.anchor: وهي أن اللعين قال للملائكة إني أسلم أن لي إلها هو خالقي وموجدي لكن لي على حكمه أسئلة

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In the reported debate, the Four-Gospel commentator gives God’s answer: Iblis does not know God, and so cannot object to any divine act.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه من سرادق العظمة والكبرياء يا إبليس أنت ما عرفتني

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reports al-Razi’s view that even all creatures together could not resolve the objections when judging by rational approval and disapproval, so every objection would remain binding.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام - الرازي - إنه لو اجتمع الأولون والآخرون من الخلائق وحكموا بتحسين العقل وتقبيحه

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors a story in which Sayf al-Dawla challenges his company with a couplet he thinks no one but Abu Firas could match, while Abu Firas is present.
rows.anchor: ثم قال الآلوسي ويعجبني ما يحكى أن سيف الدولة بن حمدان خرج يوما على جماعته فقال قد عملت بيتا

rows.speaker: أبو فراس
rows.claim: Abu Firas answers Sayf al-Dawla’s boast with a witty couplet: if Sayf is the master, then the whole matter is his.
rows.anchor: فابتدر أبو فراس قائلا قال إن كنت مالكا فلي الأمر كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba’i rejects al-Razi’s claim that the six objections are irresolvable, saying his preceding account already answers them without needing the combined effort of generations.
rows.anchor: ما مر من البيان في أول الكلام السابق يصلح لدفع هذه الشبهات الست عن آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For creation in general, God is a complete agent, independent of anything that could perfect His agency; as the source of all good and mercy, His creative activity necessarily manifests that goodness.
rows.anchor: فاعل تام لمجموع ما سواه غير مفتقر في ذلك إلى متمم يتمم فاعليته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further goal is required only by an incomplete agent seeking perfection; God already possesses every good, so His own essence is His end and creation’s many benefits are secondary consequences.
rows.anchor: فإنما يحكم العقل بوجوب الغاية الزائدة على الفاعل في الفاعل الناقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not create humanity for His own benefit; the human species’ end is to transform earthly matter into a noble, elevated being whose perfection and nearness to God surpass all other beings.
rows.anchor: هو أن يخلق من المادة الأرضية الخسيسة تركيب خاص ينتهي بسلوكه في مسلك الكمال إلى جوهر علوي شريف كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material species have an end, but many individuals fail to reach it because they are exposed to opposing causes; eliminating those causes would destroy their composition and the cosmic order.
rows.anchor: وأما الأفراد و الأشخاص فكثير منها تبطل دون البلوغ إلى الكمال، وتفسد في طريق الاستكمال بعمل العلل والأسباب المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some individual failures are no defect when they allow others to attain the species’ noble end; using abundant low-grade matter to produce a little precious substance is a real gain, not waste.
rows.anchor: وصرف الكثير من المادة الخسيسة التي لا قيمة لها في تحصيل القليل من الجوهر الشريف العالي استرباح حقيقي بلا تبذير أو جزاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary aim of creating humanity is human perfection and happiness in this life and the next; some individuals’ failure is secondary and incidental because material life depends on a shared, interacting system.
rows.anchor: فالعلة الموجبة لوجود النوع الإنساني لا تريد بفعلها إلا الإنسان الكامل السائر إلى أوج السعادة في دنياه وآخرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s foreknowledge that many people will disbelieve and enter Hell neither defeats the purpose of creating humanity nor makes their creation the complete cause of their disbelief or fate.
rows.anchor: وأما علمه بأن كثيرين من أفراده يكونون كفارا مصيرهم إلى النار لا يوجب أن يختل مراده من خلقه النوع الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief’s complete cause arises only after existence through many external factors, with the person’s choice last; divine decree concerns disbelief by way of that choice, never by coercion, like a stone falling under gravity.
rows.anchor: وآخرها اختياره الذي لا يدع الفعل ينتسب إلا إليه
